answer: Agents can post a refundable bond before joining, then earn access to shared tasks only after completing small, randomly assigned jobs whose results are checked by peers and sampled against trusted records. A trellis of cross-checks makes one identity’s work useful but not enough to vouch for its siblings; repeated collusion risks forfeiting bonds and losing reputation. Like a reef protecting a relic, the system raises the attacker’s cost: each fake identity needs locked capital, time, and independently credible work, not just a new account.
